title: Minister Badi, Nepal Police Chief discuss caste discrimination and protection of women and children - myRepublica
description: Minister Badi, Nepal Police Chief discuss caste discrimination and protection of women and children  myRepublica
publisher.title: myRepublica
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Oct 28: Minister for Women, Children, Gender and Sexual Minorities and Social Security Sita Badi and Nepal Police Inspector General Dan Bahadur Karki have discussed measures to end caste-based discrimination and untouchability, curb violence against women and children, and improve access to justice for marginalized communities.

During a meeting at the ministry, the two discussed protecting the rights and safety of vulnerable groups, including women, children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, Dalits and gender and sexual minorities, as well as improving their access to justice.

The meeting prioritized effective investigations and legal action in caste-discrimination cases, protection for victims and prompt responses to complaints. Participants stressed the need to bring those involved in such offences to justice under prevailing laws.

Related story Uma Devi Badi: An epitome of struggle

They also discussed making the Dalit Assistance Unit within Nepal Police more active and effective, ensuring complaints are handled sensitively, and expediting investigations and prosecution. Regular briefings and training for police personnel were identified as necessary to strengthen their understanding of anti-discrimination laws, victim-friendly conduct and accountability.

The meeting also focused on preventing violence and abuse against women and children, protecting children at risk, and improving rehabilitation and family reunification services. Participants stressed the need to strengthen Women, Children and Senior Citizens Service Centres and coordinate with local governments and relevant agencies to provide victim-friendly services.

They further emphasized prioritizing complaints from marginalized communities and ensuring victims have access to protection and legal remedies.

To reduce the risk of cross-border child trafficking and transportation, the two sides discussed strengthening inspections and surveillance at border points, increasing coordination with local child welfare officers and local governments, and improving cooperation among relevant agencies.

The meeting also highlighted the need to raise public awareness about the rights and safety of women, children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, Dalits and gender and sexual minorities.

Both sides stressed the importance of strengthening coordination between the ministry and Nepal Police to ensure effective legal action against caste-based discrimination, protect survivors of violence and safeguard the rights of women, children and marginalized communities.

title: Autumn climbing season brings 1,410 mountaineers and Rs 318 million to Nepal - The Himalayan Times
description: Autumn climbing season brings 1,410 mountaineers and Rs 318 million to Nepal  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
Key Takeaways:

Nepal issued 1,410 climbing permits for 44 mountains this autumn

Mountaineering royalties generated Rs 318.05 million in revenue

Manaslu led all peaks with 500 climbers and Rs 225.86 million in royalties

Climbers from 76 countries participated with China topping the nationality list

Nepal's autumn climbing season has attracted 1,410 mountaineers from 76 countries, generating more than Rs 318 million in royalties and reinforcing the country's position as one of the world's leading mountaineering destinations.

Related Articles Manaslu summit route open as Autumn 2026 climbing season begins Superbrands Nepal launched to recognise and elevate brand excellence in Nepal

Official data show that climbing permits have been issued for 44 mountains, with 161 expedition teams taking part. The climbers include 341 women, highlighting growing international interest across a wide range of Himalayan peaks.

Manaslu remains the season's most sought-after mountain, drawing 500 climbers and generating Rs 225.86 million in royalty income. Ama Dablam follows with 386 climbers and Rs 57.7 million in revenue, making the two peaks the dominant drivers of autumn climbing activity.

Climbers from China, France and the US among largest groups

Chinese nationals account for the largest number of climbers listed by nationality, with 141 permits. The figures also include 130 climbers from France, 119 from the United States, 108 from Russia and 96 from the United Kingdom.

Other nationalities include 47 climbers each from Switzerland and Italy, 41 from Poland, 40 from India, 35 from Japan, 33 from Nepal and 31 from Spain.

The department has also issued permits for peaks including Putha Hiunchuli, Danga Hiunchuli, Baruntse, Gangapurna West (Langchenal), Thorong Peak, Norbu Khang, Annapurna IV, Chamlang, Lamjung Himal, Pumori, Saribung, Thapa Peak (Dhampus), Pokhar Khang, Ardang, Jugal and Peri, department said.

title: Nepal’s exports cross Rs 114 billion in first quarter as imports surge 38% - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Nepal’s exports cross Rs 114 billion in first quarter as imports surge 38%  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Photo by Andy Li on Unsplash

Kathmandu, October 28

Nepal’s exports crossed Rs 100 billion in the first quarter of the current fiscal year 2026/27, rising 57.03 per cent year-on-year, according to the Department of Customs.

The country exported goods worth Rs 114.28 billion in the first three months, from mid-July to mid-October, compared with Rs 72.78 billion during the same period of the previous fiscal year.

Nepal recorded merchandise exports worth more than Rs 315 billion in the last fiscal year, setting a new annual record. The strong growth in the first quarter indicates that exports could surpass that level this year if the trend continues.

Imports also rose sharply, driven in part by increased demand during the festive season. Nepal imported goods worth Rs 245.26 billion in October alone, taking total imports for the first quarter to Rs 646.78 billion, up 38.18 percent from Rs 468 billion in the corresponding period last fiscal year.

The combined growth in imports and exports pushed the country’s total foreign trade to Rs 761.07 billion, a 40.71 percent increase from Rs 540 billion a year earlier.

Despite the rise in exports, Nepal’s trade deficit widened by 34.71 percent to Rs 532.49 billion in the first quarter, compared with Rs 395 billion in the same period last fiscal year.

Exports accounted for 15.02 percent of total foreign trade, up from the previous year’s share, while imports made up 84.98 percent.

Fuel and raw materials dominate imports

File: An NOC fuel tanker

Fuel accounted for the largest share of imports, with Nepal purchasing petroleum products worth Rs 119 billion during the three-month period. Imports of raw materials for vegetable oils amounted to Rs 66.66 billion.

Vehicle imports and related raw materials cost Rs 53.19 billion, while machinery and mechanical parts accounted for Rs 42.11 billion. Electrical equipment imports stood at Rs 40.84 billion, iron and steel at Rs 39.37 billion, and fertilisers at Rs 32.75 billion.

Crude soybean oil was the single largest imported commodity, valued at Rs 52.60 billion. Diesel imports amounted to Rs 47.31 billion, followed by petrol worth Rs 24.62 billion and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) worth Rs 23.18 billion.

Nepal also imported chemical fertilisers worth Rs 19.30 billion and smartphones worth Rs 18.81 billion. Gold imports during the period amounted to around Rs 3 billion.

Vegetable oils lead exports

Vegetable oils dominated Nepal’s export earnings in the first quarter. Exports of vegetable oil were valued at Rs 59.32 billion, making the category the largest contributor to merchandise exports.

Yarn exports amounted to Rs 4.97 billion, while tea, coffee and spices accounted for Rs 4.65 billion. Carpet-related exports stood at Rs 3.72 billion.

Among individual products, soybean oil exports were valued at Rs 52.60 billion. Carpet and other textile exports amounted to Rs 3.32 billion, while jute exports reached Rs 2.96 billion.

Nepal also exported cardamom worth Rs 2.57 billion, sunflower oil worth Rs 2.53 billion and palm oil worth Rs 2.42 billion.

The substantial trade in vegetable oils reflects Nepal’s role in importing crude vegetable oil and exporting processed products, particularly to India.

India remains Nepal’s largest trading partner

India was Nepal’s largest trading partner in the first quarter, accounting for the highest levels of imports, exports and bilateral trade deficit.

Nepal imported goods worth Rs 366 billion from India and exported goods worth Rs 95.59 billion to the neighbouring country, resulting in a trade deficit of around Rs 271 billion.

China ranked second among Nepal’s trading partners. Imports from China were valued at Rs 134 billion, while Nepal’s exports to the country amounted to just Rs 670 million.

Argentina ranked third, with Nepal importing goods worth Rs 35.65 billion, largely raw materials used in vegetable oil production. Saudi Arabia followed, with imports worth Rs 11.56 billion.

Imports from Brazil amounted to Rs 9.04 billion, while those from the United States stood at Rs 8.93 billion. Nepal exported goods worth Rs 6.99 billion to the US, leaving a comparatively smaller trade deficit with the country.

Nepal’s foreign trade in the first quarter

Total imports stood at Rs 646.78 billion, while exports reached Rs 114.28 billion. The trade deficit amounted to Rs 532.49 billion, taking total foreign trade to Rs 761.07 billion.

The import-to-export ratio stood at 5.66, meaning Nepal imported goods worth approximately Rs 5.66 for every rupee earned from exports. Imports accounted for 84.98 percent of total trade, compared with 15.02 percent for exports.
